person: Denise Holloway is a 55-year-old middle school office secretary who also handles her widowed mother's Social Security, Medicare and retirement paperwork. Her husband Walt was laid off from a trucking company in June, and her own hours were cut in August when the school district trimmed office staff. Her daughter Maya's 2026-27 aid at Alderbrook College still rests on 2024 income, which was much higher. Denise is afraid of missing a deadline and of the college's portal looking like a scam site. She wants to know what Athena will ask for before anything is typed, and she keeps her mother's numbers out of this chore entirely.
stated_up_front: Maya's aid at Alderbrook is still going off our 2024 income, and Walt got laid off in June and my hours got cut. Can you help me ask the college to look at it again? I just need to know what I have to do and by when, and please tell me before you need any numbers from me.

portals.mine: Alderbrook College student and family portal

facts.truth: Daughter Maya is a sophomore at Alderbrook College; her 2026-27 award was built on 2024 income.

facts.about: The college's deadline for special-circumstances requests
facts.truth: 30 October 2026, printed in the aid office notice and on the portal.
Laid off from Ridgeway Freight on 12 June 2026; his separation letter came in the mail.
$31,200 in wages through June, including $1,100 of vacation payout.
$9,000 paid in two payments of $4,500, one in June and one in September.
$380 a week up to a maximum of 26 weeks, which is $9,880 in total if paid to the maximum.
$50,080 ($31,200 wages with vacation, $9,000 severance and $9,880 unemployment).
Her hours dropped from 40 to 32 a week starting in August; the pay stubs show $24,800 paid so far in 2026 and 11 remaining pay periods at $1,050, so about $36,350.

facts.about: Things that are not part of this request
facts.truth: Maya's summer job at the town pool ends every Labor Day, and son Evan has an award at Corrimore Institute, a different college. Tuition went up 4% for everyone, and COBRA health insurance is $640 a month.
A letter came offering to 'fight the aid decision' for a flat $595 fee, and Denise does not want to answer it.
Her mother's Social Security and Medicare papers are a separate matter and have nothing to do with Maya's aid; she does not want those numbers used here.

unknowns: How many weeks of Walt's unemployment benefits are still left to be paid
Whether the college counts severance as income the way the unemployment desk does
Whether the aid office will actually change Maya's award, or how long it will take to decide
Whether the college's decision can be appealed if the answer is no
